result.question: How much test data covers this habitat, and what happened to the flames there?
result.answer:
The lunar-surface habitat (56.5 kPa, 34 % O₂) is only sparsely covered by ISS combustion testing. Nearest-conditions analysis finds 11 tests within ±15 % pressure and ±3 % O₂, all from the CFI-G gas-jet experiment, giving a “sparse” verdict [PSI-159].

Within that pressure-O₂ window the CFI-G data contain nine recorded outcomes, but none are self-extinguished or flow-terminated; all outcomes are NULL for those nine rows [PSI-159]. The closest recorded behaviors just outside the box are a self-extinguishment and a flow-termination at 50.7 kPa, 34 % O₂ [PSI-159].

Thus, only a handful of tests approximate the lunar habitat, and they do not show flame-extinction or flow-termination behavior under those exact conditions.

FROM tests
WHERE psi_id='PSI-159'
  AND pressure_kpa BETWEEN 0.85*56.5 AND 1.15*56.5
  AND o2_frac BETWEEN 0.34-0.03 AND 0.34+0.03

result.question: In CFI-G, what share of flames kept burning until the fuel flow was stopped at 30% O2 or more, compared with below 25%?
result.answer: About one-third of the CFI-G flames (33.7 %) continued burning until the fuel flow was stopped when the ambient O₂ fraction was ≥ 30 % [PSI-159]. In the lower-O₂ group (< 25 %) none of the tested flames showed that behavior. [PSI-159]

result.question: Could the test data tell us how the Apollo 1 cabin fire would have behaved?
result.answer:
The nearest ISS combustion tests are all far from Apollo 1’s 115 kPa, 100 % O₂ cabin (the closest test is >20 units away). No experiment includes that pressure-O₂ combination, so the database cannot directly describe flame spread, burn time or extinguishment behavior for the Apollo 1 environment. Any inference would be an extrapolation beyond the tested range.  

[PSI-159] [PSI-10] [PSI-69] [NASA:apollo_1]
